description.narrative: Insatsen utgör en fortsättning och successiv utfasning av projektet Municipal Environmental Governance vars tidigare faser (MEG1 och MEG2) genomförts under de senaste 8 åren. Den tredje fasen, MEG3, är utformad som en konsolideringsfas som bygger vidare på uppnådda resultat och erfarenheter från MEG1 och MEG2. Fokus för MEG3 är att gå från pilotverksamhet och implementering till institutionalisering. Insatsen syftar till att integrera systematiska förbättringar i offentlig förvaltning och tillhandahållande av vattentjänster på lokal nivå. Arbetet baseras på ett resultatorienterat arbetssätt och prestationsbaserad styrning, vilket utgör kärnan i genomförandet. MEG3, som planeras pågå från 1 mars 2026 till 28 februari 2030, kommer fortsätta att stödja inhemska institutioner att ta fullt ansvar för reformverktyg, ramverk och praxis. Det övergripande målet är att säkerställa ett fullständigt institutionellt övertagande senast år 2030. Vid insatsens slut förväntas programmet säkerställa att institutioner på alla nivåer är utrustade, stärkta och förberedda att ta fullt ansvar för projektets resultat, vilket garanterar hållbarhet, skalbarhet och fortsatt påverkan bortom projektets livscykel.

The intervention represents a continuation and phasing out of previous phases (MEG1 and MEG2) implemented in last 8 years. Municipal Environmental Governance 3 (MEG3) is strategically designed as a consolidation phase that builds on the achievements and lessons learned from MEG 1 and 2, transitioning from piloting and implementation to institutionalization. The intervention is positioned to embed systemic improvements in local governance and water service delivery, using a resultsoriented approach and performancebased management as its core vehicle. MEG 3 (envisioned to last from 01.03. 2026 to 28.02.2030 ) will continue to support domestic institutions to assume full ownership of reform tools, frameworks, and practices, with the goal of complete institutional takeover by 2030, as an overarching goal. By the end of the intervention, the Programme is expected to ensure that institutions at all levels are equipped, empowered, and prepared to assume full ownership of the Project's outputs, thereby guaranteeing sustainability, scalability, and continued impact well beyond the Project's lifecycle.

The overarching goal of the project is to advance the democratization of local governance in Bosnia and Herzegovina, fostering more equitable, effective, and efficient public service delivery for citizens, with a particular focus on water supply and wastewater management services. By strengthening policy dialogue, regulatory frameworks, and governance reforms, the Project aims to enhance the sustainability, fairness, and effectiveness of essential local services. Considering this is the 3rd and last phase of the Project, an underlying objective of the Project is to consolidate and institutionalize the achievements made in previous phases.
In principle by the end of the intervention, the Programme is expected to ensure that institutions at all levels are equipped, empowered, and prepared to assume full ownership of the Project's outputs, thereby guaranteeing sustainability, scalability, and continued impact well beyond the Project's lifecycle. To that end, the MEG Project will prioritize fostering connections and collaboration both horizontally, between communities and vertically, between local governments and higher levels of government. This will be achieved through the promotion of intermunicipal cooperation, active knowledg sharing initiatives and platforms, and strengthened interinstitutional dialogue. Where relevant, MEG Project will seek to benefit from partnerships with credible international and domestic organizations with specific expertise in areas under the purview of the Project, such as the EU Institute for Public Administration (EIPA) and Transparency International.
